A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMVM benchmark, training dataset, and CoLVA method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMVM evaluations, component ablations, qualitative analyses, and additional model and VQA evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds candidate-count evaluations, further VQA results, source-specific analyses, and embedding visualizations.

M1.justification: The RADIO expert, object-level contrastive objective, adapter pretraining, instruction augmentation, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The expanded SAM/Re-ID annotation description elaborates segmentation and matching branches already depicted in v1 Figure 4; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds NaturalBench and VideoRefer-Bench evaluations, extending general VQA coverage to the multi-image/video setting in Table 3. The six earlier VQA benchmarks, previously in v1 Table 6, remain. The 1,510-example MMVM benchmark and 220K training dataset retain their coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 9 adds Qwen2VL-2B as the unmodified comparator for CoLVA on MME, POPE, and BLINK; v1's corresponding VQA comparison used only InternVL2-4B. The original MMVM comparator set remains in v3 Table 11 despite the shorter main table.

E3.justification: v3 introduces 4-, 8-, and 12-candidate evaluations alongside the original all-candidate setting. It also separately evaluates the existing 790 public-dataset and 720 internet examples and reports NaturalBench Q/I/G accuracies and VideoRefer-Bench average scores. These add evaluation protocols without establishing changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 replaces the attention-map diagnostic with PCA embedding comparisons (Figures 2 and 9), adds candidate-count sensitivity and source-specific generalization analyses, and supplies application examples in Figure 8. It also extends general-VQA transfer analysis to Qwen2VL. Existing component ablations and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new benchmark histograms describe dataset composition rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for reduced candidate sets, two additional VQA benchmarks, Qwen2VL general VQA, and MMVM source groups. For example, GPT-4o scores 56.76% with four candidates versus 42.65% with all candidates, reflecting different settings. Existing reported values also change: CoLVA-InternVL2-4B overall accuracy changes from 49.87 to 49.80, and Region-Region alignment accuracy from 45.83 to 40.45. The shortened LLaVA1.5-7B comparison omits its six non-CL/RP cue results.

T1.justification: Equation 1 retains the same contrastive-loss expression. Neither version provides formal propositions or proofs, and v3's additional motivation and visualization discussion introduce no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, dataset, and CoLVA contributions remain. v3 explicitly claims the first visual-correspondence dataset and benchmark for MLLMs, refocuses its headline result from CoLVA-Qwen2VL-7B to CoLVA-InternVL2-4B, and qualifies the sub-50% baseline finding to the all-candidate setting.

C2.justification: v3 explains why weak matching models can generate rationales when supplied matching annotations, elaborates the respective roles of the visual expert, contrastive learning, and training data, and interprets source-specific results as generalization evidence. It removes v1's speculative M-RoPE explanation for Qwen2VL's improvement. The crowded-scene and partial-view limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses validation-only benchmark sourcing, the 30% data budget for ablations, SAM/Re-ID annotation fallbacks, and vertical image concatenation for single-image models. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated changes to existing settings. Core implementation details remain, but the Osprey-727K pretraining-source disclosure is omitted. The abstract changes from claiming artifacts are available at a repository to promising future release.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to QDTrack, Video K-Net, NaturalBench, and VideoRefer Suite. It more explicitly distinguishes contrastive alignment between two encoders from approaches using shared tracking heads. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and dataset narrative are extensively rewritten, and Section 3 reverses the dataset/benchmark order. General VQA and cross-model studies move into the main text, while failure analysis and implementation material move into reorganized appendices. These are substantial structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The radar chart and attention-map figure are removed; PCA plots, benchmark histograms, and application illustrations are added. The main results table is redesigned around candidate counts, while the original full comparison moves to appendix Table 11. Several other tables and figures are relocated or condensed.

improvement.justification: The added candidate-count, multi-image VQA, and source-specific evaluations strengthen the evidence, while validation-split and ablation-budget disclosures improve interpretability. These gains are moderated by unresolved reporting inconsistencies: v3 Tables 1 and 11 disagree on CoLVA's CL/RP scores, and Table 10 retains 49.87 overall accuracy versus 49.80 elsewhere. The weaker artifact-release statement also limits the reproducibility benefit.
